props.text: New lists at the top of the page document, beside the maps, rewritten in place each round. Each entry keeps its own change lines. Gives: one file holds the whole picture, shown or not, and a session without a page reads the same file. Costs: a new file version (version 2), and new checks that an old change line never changes.

Each round writes every section again as a new card that carries the old one. Gives: no new kind of record. Costs: every section is re-sent every round, its change list is the card history (folded today), and the end check must dig stories and examples out of card text.

One Markdown file per section, plus one file of questions for others; the page document points to them. Gives: files a person can edit by hand. Costs: 2 places to keep in step, a parser per file, and notes still land on page elements, not on the files.
This is the stored shape of every future page. A wrong call outlives the feature, so you sign it later in the draft. Every later card rests on this pick.

props.text:
My reading, which holds if the first card picks A:

- Each link is stored on the side that points: a section holds the sections it links to, a question holds its sections and the one question it waits on, an example holds the stories it covers.
- Each section, question and example holds its own change lines. A change line names its cause: your note, an answer to a question, an answer from someone else (with the role), or a finding of mine.
- A note lands on a section, a question, a card, a map or the banner, as today; the note table already holds every note of the session.
- A reply answers exactly 1 note on a new page. Today 1 reply may name several notes.
- A card can propose a question for others, or hold the assumption for one.

Accept, or note a link that is wrong.
